subproblems.title: Hausdorff measure under the dilation η_{x,λ}
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, x ∈ ℝ^P, λ > 0 and η = η_{x,λ}. Then (i) Hⁿ(η(s)) = ofReal(λ^{−n})·Hⁿ(s) for every s ⊆ ℝ^P, and (ii) the push-forward measure satisfies η_#Hⁿ = ofReal(λⁿ)·Hⁿ (i.e. Hⁿ(η⁻¹(B)) = λⁿHⁿ(B) for every Borel B), where Hⁿ = μHE[n].
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (x : Euclid P) (lam : ℝ), 0 < lam → (∀ s : Set (Euclid P), μHE[n] (dilation x lam '' s) = ENNReal.ofReal (lam⁻¹ ^ n) * μHE[n] s) ∧ Measure.map (dilation x lam) (μHE[n] : Measure (Euclid P)) = ENNReal.ofReal (lam ^ n) • (μHE[n] : Measure (Euclid P))

Source: parent proof step 0(i); Hⁿ is Mathlib's normalized Euclidean Hausdorff measure μHE[n]. Here η = η_{x,λ} = dilation x λ, η(y) = −λ⁻¹x + λ⁻¹y = λ⁻¹(y − x), and ι(z) := x + λz.
1. For every s ⊆ ℝ^P, η(s) = τ(λ⁻¹·s), where λ⁻¹·s = {λ⁻¹y : y ∈ s} and τ(z) := −λ⁻¹x + z, because η(y) = −λ⁻¹x + λ⁻¹y.
2. τ is an isometry of ℝ^P (a translation), and Hausdorff measures are invariant under isometries (Mathlib Isometry.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_image): Hⁿ(τ(E)) = Hⁿ(E) for every E ⊆ ℝ^P. Hence Hⁿ(η(s)) = Hⁿ(λ⁻¹·s).
3. Homogeneity: for r ≠ 0 and every E ⊆ ℝ^P, Hⁿ(r·E) = |r|ⁿ·Hⁿ(E) (Mathlib Measure.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_smul₀: μHE[d](r • E) = ‖r‖₊^d • μHE[d](E); the map y ↦ ry multiplies the diameter of every covering set by |r|, so every δ-approximating sum for Hⁿ is multiplied by |r|ⁿ). With r = λ⁻¹ > 0 the factor is (λ⁻¹)ⁿ = λ^{−n}, which as an element of [0,∞] is ofReal(λ^{−n}). With step 2 this proves (i): Hⁿ(η(s)) = ofReal(λ^{−n})·Hⁿ(s) for every s ⊆ ℝ^P.
4. Proof of (ii). η is continuous, hence Borel measurable, so (η_#Hⁿ)(B) = Hⁿ(η⁻¹(B)) for every Borel B. Since η is a bijection with inverse ι(z) = x + λz, η⁻¹(B) = ι(B). Moreover ι = η_{x',λ'} with x' := −λ⁻¹x and λ' := λ⁻¹ > 0, because η_{x',λ'}(z) = −λ'⁻¹x' + λ'⁻¹z = −λ·(−λ⁻¹x) + λz = x + λz. By (i) applied to (x', λ'), Hⁿ(ι(B)) = ofReal(λ'^{−n})·Hⁿ(B) = ofReal(λⁿ)·Hⁿ(B). Thus η_#Hⁿ and ofReal(λⁿ)·Hⁿ agree on all Borel sets and are therefore equal measures (Measure.ext). This holds for every n, including n = 0. ∎
Formalization notes (this exact statement was proved in a scratch build): with `open scoped Pointwise`, η '' s = (fun z => −(λ⁻¹ • x) + z) '' (λ⁻¹ • s) by image_smul and image_image; isometry_add_left; ENNReal.smul_def, ENNReal.ofReal_coe_nnreal, abs_of_pos; for (ii) Measure.ext, Measure.map_apply, Measure.smul_apply and the set identity dilation x λ ⁻¹' s = dilation (−(λ⁻¹ • x)) λ⁻¹ '' s, then (i) for (−(λ⁻¹ • x), λ⁻¹) and inv_inv.
proof_key_steps: η(s) is a translate of λ⁻¹·s; Hⁿ is invariant under translations (isometries).
Hⁿ(r·E) = |r|ⁿHⁿ(E) (euclideanHausdorffMeasure_smul₀) with r = λ⁻¹ gives (i).
η⁻¹(B) = η_{−λ⁻¹x,λ⁻¹}(B), so (i) for the inverse dilation gives (η_#Hⁿ)(B) = λⁿHⁿ(B) on Borel sets, hence (ii).

subproblems.title: Test forms correspond under η_{x,λ}, and η_{x,λ#}T(ω) = λ^{−n}T(ω∘η)
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, U ⊆ ℝ^P an arbitrary subset, x ∈ ℝ^P, λ > 0 and η = η_{x,λ} (η(y) = λ⁻¹(y − x), Contract `dilation x λ`). Then (a) for every ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(η(U)) there is ω' ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) with ω'(y) = ω(η(y)) for all y ∈ ℝ^P; (b) for every ω' ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) there is ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(η(U)) with ω'(y) = ω(η(y)) for all y; (c) for every T ∈ 𝒟_n(U) and all ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(η(U)), ω' ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) with ω'(y) = ω(η(y)) for all y, the blow-up satisfies η_{x,λ#}T(ω) = λ^{−n}·T(ω'). Here 𝒟ⁿ(V) = TestFormOn V n and η_{x,λ#}T = blowUp T x λ.

Source: parent proof step 0(ii) (pullback by η_{x,λ}); Simon Ch. 6, 2.23 (push-forward f_#T(ω) = T(f^#ω), chapter-06.txt lines 405–418).
Conventions. ℝ^P = Euclid P. For x ∈ ℝ^P and λ > 0, η := η_{x,λ} = dilation x λ, η(y) = −λ⁻¹x + λ⁻¹y = λ⁻¹(y − x), and ι(z) := x + λz. For V ⊆ ℝ^P (any subset), 𝒟ⁿ(V) = TestFormOn V n is the set of C^∞ maps ω : ℝ^P → Λⁿ(ℝ^P) (n-covectors) with compact topological support tsupport ω ⊆ V; elements of 𝒟ⁿ(V) are determined by their underlying forms. η_#Y := η_{x,λ#}Y = blowUp Y x λ for Y ∈ 𝒟_n(U). By the Contract definition of blowUp, for T ∈ 𝒟_n(U) and ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(η(U)) we have η_#T(ω) = T(ν), where ν ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) has underlying form ν(y) = ω(−λ⁻¹x + L y) ∘ L with L := λ⁻¹·id (= dilationCLM P λ), i.e. ν(y)(v₁,…,vₙ) = ω(η(y))(λ⁻¹v₁,…,λ⁻¹vₙ) (SimonGMT affinePullbackForm L (−λ⁻¹x) ω; it is a test form in η⁻¹(η(U)) and is regarded as a test form in U through the inclusion η⁻¹(η(U)) ⊆ U, which does not change the underlying form).
1. η is an affine homeomorphism of ℝ^P with inverse ι. Indeed η is the composition of y ↦ λ⁻¹y (a homeomorphism since λ⁻¹ ≠ 0) with the translation z ↦ z − λ⁻¹x, and η(ι(z)) = λ⁻¹(x + λz − x) = z, ι(η(y)) = x + λ·λ⁻¹(y − x) = y. Both η and ι are affine, hence C^∞. In particular η is injective, so η⁻¹(η(V)) = V for every V ⊆ ℝ^P.
2. Two facts about supports. Let h : ℝ^P → ℝ^P be continuous and f : ℝ^P → Λⁿ(ℝ^P). (i) tsupport(f∘h) ⊆ h⁻¹(tsupport f): the set h⁻¹(tsupport f) is closed and contains {f∘h ≠ 0} = h⁻¹{f ≠ 0}. (ii) If h is a homeomorphism and f has compact support, then f∘h has compact support: h⁻¹(tsupport f) is compact (it is the image of the compact set tsupport f under the continuous inverse of h), and tsupport(f∘h) is a closed subset of it by (i).
3. Proof of (a). Let ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(η(U)) and put ω' := ω∘η. Then ω' is C^∞ (composition of C^∞ maps), has compact support by 2(ii), and tsupport ω' ⊆ η⁻¹(tsupport ω) ⊆ η⁻¹(η(U)) = U by 2(i) and step 1. Hence ω' ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U), and ω'(y) = ω(η(y)) for every y by definition.
4. Proof of (b). Let ω' ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) and put ω := ω'∘ι. Then ω is C^∞, has compact support by 2(ii) (ι is a homeomorphism), and tsupport ω ⊆ ι⁻¹(tsupport ω') ⊆ ι⁻¹(U). If ι(z) ∈ U then z = η(ι(z)) ∈ η(U); hence tsupport ω ⊆ η(U) and ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(η(U)). Finally ω(η(y)) = ω'(ι(η(y))) = ω'(y) for every y.
5. Proof of (c). Let T ∈ 𝒟_n(U), ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(η(U)) and ω' ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) with ω'(y) = ω(η(y)) for all y, and let ν be the test form in the definition of η_#T(ω). Note −λ⁻¹x + L y = η(y). Fix y and v₁,…,vₙ ∈ ℝ^P and put α := ω(η(y)) ∈ Λⁿ(ℝ^P). Since α is multilinear, α(λ⁻¹v₁,…,λ⁻¹vₙ) = (∏_{i=1}^{n} λ⁻¹)·α(v₁,…,vₙ) = λ^{−n}·α(v₁,…,vₙ) (for n = 0 the empty product is 1 = λ⁰). Hence ν(y) = λ^{−n}ω(η(y)) = λ^{−n}ω'(y) for all y, so ν = λ^{−n}ω' as elements of 𝒟ⁿ(U). By linearity of T, η_#T(ω) = T(ν) = T(λ^{−n}ω') = λ^{−n}·T(ω'). This proves (a), (b), (c) for arbitrary U and n. ∎
Formalization notes (this exact statement was proved in a scratch build): unfold blowUp, then rewrite with GeometricCurrentOn.affinePushforward_apply and GeometricCurrentOn.restrictDomain_apply; reduce to an equality of underlying forms (Subtype.ext, funext, ext v) and use testFormOnInclusion_coe, affinePullbackTestOn_coe, affinePullbackForm, ContinuousAlternatingMap.compContinuousLinearMap_apply, ContinuousAlternatingMap.map_smul_univ, Finset.prod_const, Finset.card_univ, Fintype.card_fin, then map_smul and smul_eq_mul. For (a), (b) build ⟨f, h⟩ after `change IsTestForm f ∧ tsupport f ⊆ V`, using HasCompactSupport.comp_homeomorph for the homeomorphisms (Homeomorph.smulOfNeZero λ⁻¹ _).trans (Homeomorph.addLeft (−(λ⁻¹ • x))) (coercion = dilation x λ) and (Homeomorph.smulOfNeZero λ _).trans (Homeomorph.addLeft x), together with tsupport_comp_subset_preimage and Set.preimage_image_eq. Under `open scoped ENNReal` the symbol ∞ is ENNReal's top, so write the smoothness order as ((⊤ : ℕ∞) : WithTop ℕ∞).
proof_key_steps: η is an affine homeomorphism with inverse ι(z) = x + λz; composition with a homeomorphism preserves smoothness and compact support, and tsupport(f∘h) ⊆ h⁻¹(tsupport f).
(a) ω' := ω∘η is a test form with tsupport ⊆ η⁻¹(η(U)) = U.
(b) ω := ω'∘ι is a test form with tsupport ⊆ ι⁻¹(U) ⊆ η(U), and ω∘η = ω'.
(c) The pulled-back form is ω(η(y))∘(λ⁻¹·id) = λ^{−n}ω(η(y)) = λ^{−n}ω'(y) by multilinearity; linearity of T gives η_#T(ω) = λ^{−n}T(ω').

If Q is the approximate tangent space of M at y in the sense of Simon 3.1.4 (SimonGMT HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M y Q: dim Q = n and ∫_{η_{y,r}(M)} f dHⁿ → ∫_Q f dHⁿ as r ↓ 0 for every f ∈ C_c(ℝ^P)), then HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n (η(M)) (η(y)) Q.

Its accepted natural-language proof, which proves exactly this statement, follows verbatim; "parent" in it refers to its original parent node root.density_and_tangent_cones-a1.blowup_scaling-a1.

Source: Simon Ch. 3, Definition 1.4 (chapter-03.txt lines 77–86), formalized by SimonGMT HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M y Q := finrank Q = n ∧ ∀ f ∈ C_c(ℝ^P;ℝ), lim_{r→0+} ∫_{blowUpMap y r '' M} f dHⁿ = ∫_Q f dHⁿ, with blowUpMap y r w = r⁻¹•(w − y); parent proof step 2, orientation bullet (η_{z,r}(η(M)) = η_{y,λr}(M)). Here η = η_{x,λ} = dilation x λ, Hⁿ = μHE[n].
1. The condition finrank Q = n involves neither M nor the base point, so it holds for η(M) at η(y).
2. Set identity. For w ∈ ℝ^P, η(w) − η(y) = (−λ⁻¹x + λ⁻¹w) − (−λ⁻¹x + λ⁻¹y) = λ⁻¹(w − y). Hence for every r ∈ ℝ, blowUpMap(η(y), r)(η(w)) = r⁻¹λ⁻¹(w − y) = (λr)⁻¹(w − y) = blowUpMap(y, λr)(w), using (λr)⁻¹ = λ⁻¹r⁻¹ (valid in ℝ with the convention 0⁻¹ = 0). Taking images of M: blowUpMap(η(y), r)(η(M)) = blowUpMap(y, λr)(M) for all r.
3. Fix f ∈ C_c(ℝ^P;ℝ) and put g(s) := ∫_{blowUpMap(y,s)(M)} f dHⁿ. By step 2, for every r the integral ∫_{blowUpMap(η(y),r)(η(M))} f dHⁿ is literally g(λr) (same domain of integration, same integrand and same measure, so no integrability is needed for this identity).

subproblems.title: Representation transfer for dilations: λ^{−m}η_*μ with ξ(a + λ·)
subproblems.statement: Let P, m ∈ ℕ, a ∈ ℝ^P, λ > 0 and η := dilation a λ. Let X, X' ∈ 𝒟_m(ℝ^P) with X'(ω) = λ^{−m}X(ω') for all ω, ω' ∈ 𝒟^m(ℝ^P) with ω'(y) = ω(η(y)) for every y, let μ be any measure on ℝ^P (Borel σ-algebra) and ξ : ℝ^P → Λ_m(ℝ^P) (MultiVector P m) any map. If X(ω) = ∫ξ(x)(ω(x)) dμ(x) for every ω ∈ 𝒟^m(ℝ^P) (Bochner integrals, with value 0 for non-integrable integrands), then X'(ω) = ∫ξ(a + λy)(ω(y)) d(ofReal(λ^{−m})·η_*μ)(y) for every ω ∈ 𝒟^m(ℝ^P), where η_*μ = Measure.map (dilation a λ) μ.

Source: step 8 of the parent proof (representation transfer by change of variables for the measurable equivalence η), with the test form ω∘η supplied by the sibling testform_correspondence (a).
Conventions. ℝ^P = Euclid P; η := dilation a λ, η(y) = −λ⁻¹a + λ⁻¹y = λ⁻¹(y − a), λ > 0. For V ⊆ ℝ^P, 𝒟^k(V) = TestFormOn V k is the space of C^∞ k-forms ω on ℝ^P (maps to k-covectors) with compact tsupport ω ⊆ V; its elements are determined by their underlying forms. 𝒟_k(V) = GeometricCurrentOn V k. For X, X' ∈ 𝒟_k(ℝ^P), X' is a dilation of X when X'(ω) = λ^{−k}X(ω') for all ω, ω' ∈ 𝒟^k(ℝ^P) with ω'(y) = ω(η(y)) for every y. η_#Y := η_{a,λ#}Y = blowUp Y a λ ∈ 𝒟_k(η(U)) for Y ∈ 𝒟_k(U). Fix ω ∈ 𝒟^m(ℝ^P).
1. η is onto ℝ^P: for y ∈ ℝ^P, η(a + λy) = −λ⁻¹a + λ⁻¹(a + λy) = −λ⁻¹a + λ⁻¹a + (λ⁻¹λ)y = y because λ ≠ 0. Hence ℝ^P ⊆ η(ℝ^P), i.e. η(ℝ^P) = ℝ^P, so every ω ∈ 𝒟^k(ℝ^P) is also an element of 𝒟^k(η(ℝ^P)) with the same underlying form (tsupport ω ⊆ ℝ^P ⊆ η(ℝ^P); SimonGMT testFormOnInclusion), and every element of 𝒟^k(η(ℝ^P)) is an element of 𝒟^k(ℝ^P) with the same underlying form. Let ω₁ ∈ 𝒟^m(η(ℝ^P)) be ω regarded in η(ℝ^P). By testform_correspondence (a) (U = ℝ^P, x = a, n = m) there is ω' ∈ 𝒟^m(ℝ^P) with ω'(y) = ω₁(η(y)) = ω(η(y)) for all y.
2. By the dilation property for the pair ω, ω' and the representation of X: X'(ω) = λ^{−m}X(ω') = λ^{−m}∫ξ(x)(ω'(x)) dμ(x) = λ^{−m}∫ξ(x)(ω(η(x))) dμ(x), the last step because the integrands agree at every x.
3. η is a homeomorphism of ℝ^P: it is y ↦ λ⁻¹y (a homeomorphism since λ⁻¹ ≠ 0; Homeomorph.smulOfNeZero) followed by the translation z ↦ −λ⁻¹a + z (Homeomorph.addLeft), and this composite is exactly dilation a λ. Hence η is a measurable embedding (Homeomorph.measurableEmbedding). For a measurable embedding f, every measure μ and every g : ℝ^P → ℝ, ∫g d(f_*μ) = ∫g∘f dμ (Mathlib MeasurableEmbedding.integral_map; no integrability or measurability of g is needed, both sides being 0 in the non-integrable case).

5. For c ∈ [0,∞] and any measure ν, ∫g d(c·ν) = c.toReal·∫g dν (Mathlib integral_smul_measure). With c = ofReal(λ^{−m}) and λ^{−m} ≥ 0, c.toReal = λ^{−m}. Hence ∫ξ(a + λy)(ω(y)) d(ofReal(λ^{−m})·η_*μ)(y) = λ^{−m}∫g d(η_*μ) = λ^{−m}∫ξ(x)(ω(η(x))) dμ(x) = X'(ω) by steps 2 and 4. ∎

η is a homeomorphism, hence a measurable embedding; ∫g d(η_*μ) = ∫g∘η dμ for every g (MeasurableEmbedding.integral_map).
With g(y) = ξ(a + λy)(ω(y)) and a + λη(x) = x, g∘η = ξ(·)(ω∘η); integral_smul_measure with (ofReal λ^{−m}).toReal = λ^{−m} finishes.

subproblems.title: Mass scaling for dilations: M_{η(W)}(X′) = λ^{−m}M_W(X)
